# Overview

**Module 3: Repeat detection**

This module handles:

1. Finding each repeat tract in every read, between the two flank alignments and up to `rpt_flank_pad` bases into each flank (so a tract is measured in full even where the aligner placed a flank boundary inside it)
2. Counting each tract three ways: **full** (tract length / motif length, including any interruption inside the tract), **match** (exact motif units) and **pure** (longest uninterrupted run)
3. Recording the sequence between consecutive tracts (e.g. the CAACAGCCGCCA interruption between CAG and CCG)
4. Combined measures defined from two or more tracts (sum of units, or span from first tract start to last tract end)
5. Optional removal of reads with outlying combined flank length

**Tracts in this run:**

```{r tract_table, echo=FALSE}
dt_compact(tracts %>% dplyr::transmute(tract, motif, reference = basename(path_ref), order_in_reference = order_in_ref,
                                primary_count = count_method, min_repeats, start_perfect_repeats, end_perfect_repeats,
                                max_gap, max_tract_gap, flank_pad, reads_without_tract = na_handling))
if (nrow(composites)) dt_compact(composites %>% dplyr::transmute(measure = name, tracts, mode), caption = "Combined measures")
```

The first tract (**`r primary`**) is the primary measure: it is used for allele clustering, waterfalls and UMI allele assignment, and its ranges in the settings file apply to every other measure that has no ranges of its own.

**Outputs:**

- `03_repeat_detection/repeat_detection.xlsx` – detection rates, count-method agreement, between-tract sequences
- `03_repeat_detection/read_repeat_counts/{sample}.tsv.gz` – one row per read with every count of every tract
- `module_data/03_repeat_detection.RData` – per-read lengths for Modules 4–7 (`alignment_counts_slim` keeps the layout older scripts use)

---

# Finding tracts

```{r detect}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
safe_load_module(file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "02_alignment.RData"), 2)
alignments <- module2_output$alignments; refs <- module2_output$refs
ref_of <- function(path) names(refs)[vapply(refs, function(r) identical(normalizePath(r$path), path), logical(1))]
group_tables <- list()
slim <- NULL
for (g in unique(tracts$ref_group)) {
  tg <- tracts[tracts$ref_group == g, ]
  rid <- ref_of(tg$path_ref[1])
  a <- alignments[[rid]]
  per_sample <- split(a, a$file_stem)
  res <- apply_fn(names(per_sample), function(s) {
    aln <- per_sample[[s]]
    rt <- process_sample_repeats(aln, tg)
    if (primary %in% tg$tract) rt <- cbind(rt, primary_segments(aln, rt, primary))
    rt
  })
  gt <- rbindlist(res, fill = TRUE)
  setnames(gt, c("ref_id", "strand"), paste0(c("ref_id_", "strand_"), g))
  group_tables[[as.character(g)]] <- gt
}
rm(res, per_sample)
read_tracts <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("file_stem", "qname"), all = TRUE), group_tables)
n_groups <- length(group_tables)
timings["Tract detection"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

```{r na_handling}
# Composites first, so a read missing one of the tracts has no composite value
read_tracts <- compute_composites(read_tracts, composites, tracts)
# Reads that aligned to a tract's reference but where no tract was found
for (k in seq_len(nrow(tracts))) {
  t <- tracts$tract[k]
  aligned <- !is.na(read_tracts[[paste0("ref_id_", tracts$ref_group[k])]])
  none <- aligned & is.na(read_tracts[[paste0(t, "_start")]])
  read_tracts[, paste0(t, "_found") := ifelse(aligned, !none, NA)]
  if (tracts$na_handling[k] == "convert_to_zero") {
    for (m in c("full", "match", "pure")) set(read_tracts, which(none), paste0(t, "_", m), 0)
  }
}
if (n_groups > 1 && nrow(composites) && any(composites$mode == "span")) {
  # Spans across references are only defined when both alignments put the read on the same strand
  sc <- paste0("strand_", unique(tracts$ref_group))
  diff_strand <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(sc[-1], function(s) read_tracts[[s]] != read_tracts[[sc[1]]]))
  for (nm in composites$name[composites$mode == "span"]) set(read_tracts, which(diff_strand), nm, NA_real_)
}
drop_primary <- primary_drop <- NULL
if (any(tracts$na_handling == "filter")) {
  for (t in tracts$tract[tracts$na_handling == "filter"]) read_tracts <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE]
}
measures <- rbind(
  data.frame(measure = tracts$tract, type = "tract", motif = tracts$motif, count_method = tracts$count_method,
             definition = paste0(tracts$motif, " tract, ", tracts$count_method, " count")),
  if (nrow(composites)) data.frame(measure = composites$name, type = "combined", motif = NA, count_method = composites$mode,
                                   definition = ifelse(composites$mode == "sum", paste0(gsub("\\+", " + ", composites$tracts), " (units added)"),
                                                       paste0(composites$tracts, " (start of first to end of last)"))))
value_col <- function(m) { k <- match(m, tracts$tract); if (is.na(k)) m else paste0(m, "_", tracts$count_method[k]) }
```

## Detection rate

Each point is one sample: the percentage of its aligned reads in which **no** tract was found (so lower is better, and the axis is not capped at 100%). A tract is missing when no run of at least `min_repeats` units overlaps the region between the flanks; for a normal-length allele this should be very rare, so a high rate points to off-target product or a reference that does not match the amplicon. Detection rates per sample are in the table below and in `repeat_detection.xlsx`.

```{r detection_plot, fig.height=5}
det <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  read_tracts[!is.na(get(paste0(t, "_found"))), .(tract = t, aligned_reads = .N, with_tract = sum(get(paste0(t, "_found")))), by = file_stem]
}))[, detection_rate := with_tract / aligned_reads]
miss <- 1 - det$detection_rate
# Decimal places from the size of the largest value, so tiny rates are not all printed as 0.000%
miss_digits <- if (max(miss) > 0) max(1, -floor(log10(max(miss) * 100)) + 1) else 1
p_det <- ggplot(det, aes(tract, 1 - detection_rate)) + box_points_mean(digits = miss_digits, percent = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Tract", y = "Aligned reads with no tract found", title = "Reads without a tract, per sample",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s of %s aligned reads had no tract (%s)", comma(sum(det$aligned_reads - det$with_tract)),
                          comma(sum(det$aligned_reads)), percent(1 - sum(det$with_tract) / sum(det$aligned_reads), 10^-miss_digits))) + theme_bw()
print(p_det); save_plot(p_det, file.path(plots_dir, "detection_rate.png"), 7, 5)
```

```{r pairing, eval=n_groups > 1, results='asis'}
paired <- read_tracts[, .(reads = .N, all_tracts = sum(Reduce(`&`, lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) !is.na(get(paste0(t, "_found"))))))), by = file_stem]
cat(sprintf("\n\nTracts come from %d references. %s of %s reads (%.1f%%) aligned to every reference and so carry every tract.\n\n",
            n_groups, comma(sum(paired$all_tracts)), comma(sum(paired$reads)), 100 * sum(paired$all_tracts) / sum(paired$reads)))
```

---

# Counting methods

For each read and tract, **full** counts every base of the tract (so an interruption or a sequencing error inside it adds units rather than splitting it), **match** counts exact motif units, and **pure** is the longest uninterrupted run. They agree for a clean tract. Where they differ, the tract contains either a real interruption or a sequencing error. The comparisons below are made read by read, so they need no assumption about alleles, controls or how similar the alleles of a tract are.

```{r method_agreement}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
agree <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  f <- paste0(t, "_full"); m <- paste0(t, "_match"); pu <- paste0(t, "_pure")
  read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE,
              .(tract = t, reads = .N, all_agree = mean(get(f) == get(m) & get(m) == get(pu)),
                full_ne_match = mean(get(f) != get(m)), full_ne_pure = mean(get(f) != get(pu)),
                mean_full_minus_match = mean(get(f) - get(m)), mean_full_minus_pure = mean(get(f) - get(pu)),
                interrupted = mean(grepl(",", get(paste0(t, "_structure"))))), by = file_stem]
}))
# The same comparison by tract length (full count), per sample: the bin is 1 unit for
# short tracts and 5 units where a tract spans more than 40 units
by_len <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  f <- paste0(t, "_full"); m <- paste0(t, "_match"); pu <- paste0(t, "_pure")
  d <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, .(file_stem, full = get(f), match = get(m), pure = get(pu))]
  span <- diff(stats::quantile(d$full, c(0.001, 0.999), na.rm = TRUE))
  w <- if (span > 40) 5 else 1
  d[, length_bin := floor(full / w) * w]
  d[, .(tract = t, bin_width = w, reads = .N, full_ne_match = mean(full != match), full_ne_pure = mean(full != pure),
        mean_full_minus_pure = mean(full - pure)), by = .(file_stem, length_bin)]
}))
setorder(by_len, tract, file_stem, length_bin)
```

## Disagreement by tract length

Each grey line is one sample: the share of its reads, at each tract length (full count), whose **match** or **pure** count differs from **full**; the coloured line is the cohort (all reads pooled). Lengths with fewer than 20 reads in a sample are left out of that sample's line, and lines break across lengths with no reads. If disagreement comes from sequencing errors it rises steadily with length, because a longer tract has more bases in which an error can fall: with about 0.1–0.2% errors per base inside a repeat, a 14-unit tract is almost always read cleanly, but most 120-unit (360 bp) tracts carry at least one error. **pure** then measures the distance between errors rather than the tract, which is why **full** is the default. A real interruption instead gives a step at the lengths of the allele that carries it.

```{r agreement_by_length, fig.height=5.5}
bl_long <- melt(by_len, id.vars = c("file_stem", "tract", "length_bin", "bin_width", "reads"),
                measure.vars = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"), variable.name = "method", value.name = "share")
bl_long[, method := factor(method, levels = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"), labels = c("match differs from full", "pure differs from full"))]
pooled <- by_len[, .(full_ne_match = sum(full_ne_match * reads) / sum(reads), full_ne_pure = sum(full_ne_pure * reads) / sum(reads), reads = sum(reads)),
                 by = .(tract, length_bin)][reads >= 50]
pooled_long <- melt(pooled, id.vars = c("tract", "length_bin", "reads"), measure.vars = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"),
                    variable.name = "method", value.name = "share")
pooled_long[, method := factor(method, levels = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"), labels = levels(bl_long$method))]
# Fill in empty lengths as NA so that lines break across gaps instead of joining distant lengths
fill_gaps <- function(d, keys) {
  grid <- d[, .(length_bin = seq(min(length_bin), max(length_bin), by = bin_width[1])), by = keys]
  d[grid, on = c(keys, "length_bin")]
}
bl_plot <- fill_gaps(bl_long[reads >= 20], c("tract", "method", "file_stem"))
pooled_long[, bin_width := by_len$bin_width[match(tract, by_len$tract)]]
pooled_plot <- fill_gaps(pooled_long, c("tract", "method"))
# Each bin is drawn at its centre (a 5-unit bin starting at 10 covers 10-14)
bl_plot[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]; pooled_plot[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]
p_agree <- ggplot(bl_plot, aes(x, share)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = file_stem), colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = pooled_plot, aes(colour = method), linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(method ~ tract, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4daf4a", "#e41a1c"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Tract length, full count (units)", y = "Reads whose count differs from full",
       title = "Counting-method disagreement by tract length",
       subtitle = "Grey = one line per sample (bins with at least 20 reads); colour = all reads pooled") + theme_bw()
print(p_agree); save_plot(p_agree, file.path(plots_dir, "count_method_agreement.png"), 10, 6)
```

## Counts against each other

Each panel compares a count with **full** read by read (a random subset of up to 2,000 reads per sample), shaded by how many reads fall in each cell. Reads on the dashed diagonal have the same count by both methods. **match** stays on or just below the diagonal, because a single wrong base costs at most one unit; **pure** falls below it whenever the tract is broken, by up to half the tract for a single break near the middle.

```{r count_scatter, fig.height=5.5}
set.seed(123)
cs <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  d <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, .(file_stem, full = get(paste0(t, "_full")),
                    match = get(paste0(t, "_match")), pure = get(paste0(t, "_pure")))]
  d <- d[, .SD[sample(.N, min(.N, 2000))], by = file_stem]
  rbind(d[, .(tract = t, full, other = match, method = "match")], d[, .(tract = t, full, other = pure, method = "pure")])
}))
p_cs <- ggplot(cs, aes(full, other)) + geom_bin2d(binwidth = c(1, 1)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", labels = comma, name = "Reads") +
  facet_wrap(tract ~ method, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(method = c(match = "match against full", pure = "pure against full"))) +
  labs(x = "full count (units)", y = "match or pure count (units)", title = "Counting methods against the full count, per read") + theme_bw()
print(p_cs); save_plot(p_cs, file.path(plots_dir, "count_methods_scatter.png"), 10, 5.5)
```

## Where the tract is broken

For reads whose tract is broken (two or more runs), the position of each break as a fraction of the way along the tract (0 = the 5' start, 1 = the 3' end), from up to 2,000 broken reads per sample. **Sequencing errors** give a flat distribution, because they can fall anywhere; a **real interruption** gives a sharp peak at the same position in read after read, and would mean **pure** or **match** is the more meaningful count for that tract. Fewer breaks appear within the first and last two units, because a tract must start and end with `rpt_start_perfect_repeats` / `rpt_end_perfect_repeats` perfect units; each break is known only to the nearest unit, so it is placed at random within that unit; without this, short tracts (with only a few possible break positions) would give a comb of spikes that looks like interruptions.

```{r break_positions, fig.height=4.5}
set.seed(123)
bp <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  d <- read_tracts[grepl(",", get(paste0(t, "_structure"))), .(file_stem, s = get(paste0(t, "_structure")))]
  d <- d[, .SD[sample(.N, min(.N, 2000))], by = file_stem]
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
  runs <- lapply(strsplit(d$s, ",", fixed = TRUE), as.numeric)
  # A break is known only to the unit, so it is placed at random within that unit; otherwise
  # short tracts (only a few possible positions) give a comb of spikes that looks like interruptions
  pos <- lapply(runs, function(r) (head(cumsum(r), -1) - stats::runif(length(r) - 1)) / sum(r))
  data.table(tract = t, position = unlist(pos))
}))
if (nrow(bp)) {
  p_bp <- ggplot(bp, aes(position)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, fill = "#377eb8") +
    facet_wrap(~ tract, scales = "free_y") + scale_x_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(x = "Position of the break along the tract", y = "Breaks", title = "Where broken tracts are broken",
         subtitle = "Flat = sequencing errors; a sharp peak = an interruption in the sequence") + theme_bw()
  print(p_bp); save_plot(p_bp, file.path(plots_dir, "break_positions.png"), 10, 4.5)
} else cat("No broken tracts.\n")
```

```{r agreement_table}
dt_full(merge(det, agree, by = c("file_stem", "tract")), caption = "Detection and counting-method agreement per sample and tract", digits = 4)
dt_full(by_len, caption = "Counting-method agreement per sample, tract and tract length (full count bin)", digits = 4)
timings["Counting methods"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Modal length by counting method

The modal (most common) length of each tract per sample, calculated with each counting method over all reads. Where a sample has two alleles this is usually the more abundant one, so the length plots above are the better guide to how the methods differ; per-range modal, mean and median by method are in Module 6.

```{r modal_by_method}
modal_method <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, {
    mo <- function(x) { tb <- table(x); as.numeric(names(tb)[which.max(tb)]) }
    .(tract = t, modal_full = mo(get(paste0(t, "_full"))), modal_match = mo(get(paste0(t, "_match"))), modal_pure = mo(get(paste0(t, "_pure"))))
  }, by = file_stem]
}))
dt_full(modal_method, caption = "Modal tract length per sample by counting method (all reads)")
```

# Sequence between tracts

```{r between, eval=any(grepl("^between_", names(read_tracts))), fig.height=5}
bcols <- grep("^between_", names(read_tracts), value = TRUE)
between <- rbindlist(lapply(bcols, function(b) {
  d <- read_tracts[, .(file_stem, sequence = get(b))][!is.na(sequence)]
  d[, .(n = .N), by = .(file_stem, sequence)][, `:=`(junction = sub("^between_", "", b), prop = n / sum(n)), by = file_stem]
}))
between[sequence == "", sequence := "(none: tracts adjacent)"]
top <- between[, .(reads = sum(n), samples = uniqueN(file_stem)), by = .(junction, sequence)][order(junction, -reads)][, head(.SD, 6), by = junction]
between[, label := ifelse(sequence %in% top$sequence, sequence, "other")]
p_between <- ggplot(between[, .(prop = sum(prop)), by = .(file_stem, junction, label)], aes(label, prop)) +
  box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) + facet_wrap(~ junction, scales = "free_x") + coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads in the sample", title = "Sequence between consecutive tracts",
       subtitle = "One point per sample: the share of its reads carrying each sequence (the six most common across the cohort shown)") + theme_bw()
print(p_between); save_plot(p_between, file.path(plots_dir, "between_tract_sequences.png"), 10, 5)
```

The sequence between the CAG and CCG tracts identifies the interruption structure of each read: `CAACAGCCGCCA` is the canonical allele, a duplicated `CAACAG` gives DOI, and an allele with no CAA or CCA interruption has the tracts adjacent. Per-sample proportions are in `repeat_detection.xlsx`.

---

# Flank length

The combined length of the two flanks (everything aligned outside the primary tract) should be nearly constant within a sample. Each point is one sample: the share of its reads whose combined flank length is at its modal value, or 1–10, 11–50 or more than 50 bp away from it. Small differences (1–10 bp) are usual: the flanks include everything outside the tract, so UMI length, indels near the read ends and where the aligner starts each flank all vary by a few bases. Large deviations are chimeras, truncated reads or boundary shifts. At HTT a sample can legitimately carry two flank lengths when its alleles differ in the CCG tract, which is why the optional filter is off by default.

```{r flank_qc, fig.height=5}
fq <- read_tracts[!is.na(left), .(file_stem, qname, flank_total = nchar(left) + nchar(right))]
fq[, modal := { tb <- table(flank_total); as.numeric(names(tb)[which.max(tb)]) }, by = file_stem]
fq[, dev := abs(flank_total - modal)]
fq[, band := cut(dev, c(-1, 0, 10, 50, Inf), labels = c("at modal", "1-10 bp", "11-50 bp", ">50 bp"))]
fband <- fq[, .N, by = .(file_stem, band)][, prop := N / sum(N), by = file_stem]
p_flank <- ggplot(fband, aes(band, prop)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) + scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = "Distance from the sample's modal combined flank length", y = "Reads in the sample", title = "Combined flank length, per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_flank); save_plot(p_flank, file.path(plots_dir, "flank_length.png"), 8, 5)
if (isTRUE(params$rm_flank_length_outliers)) {
  fe <- fq[, .(q1 = quantile(flank_total, 0.25), q3 = quantile(flank_total, 0.75)), by = file_stem][, iqr := q3 - q1]
  fq <- fe[fq, on = "file_stem"]
  drop <- fq[iqr > 0 & (flank_total < q1 - params$flank_iqr_multiplier * iqr | flank_total > q3 + params$flank_iqr_multiplier * iqr), .(file_stem, qname)]
  read_tracts <- read_tracts[!drop, on = .(file_stem, qname)]
  cat(sprintf("Flank length filter (%.1f x IQR) removed %s reads.\n", params$flank_iqr_multiplier, comma(nrow(drop))))
}
```

# Save output

```{r save}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
lengths <- rbindlist(lapply(measures$measure, function(m) {
  vc <- value_col(m)
  read_tracts[!is.na(get(vc)), .(file_stem, qname, measure = m, length = as.numeric(get(vc)))]
}))
alignment_counts_slim <- read_tracts[!is.na(left), .(file_stem, qname, left, mid, right,
  repeat_count = get(value_col(primary)), repeat_count_full = get(paste0(primary, "_full")),
  repeat_count_match = get(paste0(primary, "_match")), repeat_count_pure = get(paste0(primary, "_pure")),
  repeat_count_tracts = get(paste0(primary, "_structure")))]
count_cols <- c(unlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) paste0(t, c("_full", "_match", "_pure", "_structure")))),
                grep("^between_", names(read_tracts), value = TRUE), composites$name)
if (isTRUE(params$export_read_counts)) {
  rc_dir <- file.path(rep_dir, "read_repeat_counts"); dir.create(rc_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (s in unique(read_tracts$file_stem)) {
    x <- read_tracts[file_stem == s, c("qname", count_cols), with = FALSE]
    setnames(x, "qname", "read_id")
    # legacy columns for scripts written against Duke 2.x
    x[, `:=`(repeat_count_full = get(paste0(primary, "_full")), repeat_count_match = get(paste0(primary, "_match")),
             repeat_count_tracts = get(paste0(primary, "_structure")))]
    fwrite(x, file.path(rc_dir, paste0(s, ".tsv.gz")), sep = "\t")
  }
}
read_tracts[, c("left", "right") := NULL]
module3_output <- list(read_tracts = read_tracts, lengths = lengths, measures = measures, primary = primary,
                       tracts = tracts, composites = composites, alignment_counts_slim = alignment_counts_slim,
                       detection = det, method_agreement = agree, method_by_length = by_len, modal_by_method = modal_method,
                       between = if (exists("between")) between else NULL, hash = params$module_hash)
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "03_repeat_detection.RData")
save(module3_output, file = output_path)
write_excel_function(list(tracts = tracts, measures = measures, detection = det, method_agreement = agree,
                          method_by_length = by_len,
                          modal_by_method = modal_method, between_tracts = module3_output$between), xlsx_path)
timings["Save"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

**`r comma(uniqueN(lengths[measure == primary, qname]))`** reads with a `r primary` length passed to Modules 4–7.

```{r diagnostics}
timing_df <- build_timing_table(timings)
manifest <- build_manifest(module3_output, c(
  read_tracts = "One row per read: coordinates, counts, sequence and structure of every tract; between-tract sequences; combined measures",
  lengths = "Long table (file_stem, qname, measure, length) of each measure's primary count, used by Modules 4-7",
  measures = "The measures (tracts and combined) and how each is counted", primary = "Name of the primary tract",
  tracts = "Resolved tracts table", composites = "Combined-measure definitions",
  alignment_counts_slim = "Primary tract per read in the Duke 2.x layout (left, mid, right, repeat_count_*)",
  detection = "Tract detection per sample", method_agreement = "Counting-method agreement per sample",
  method_by_length = "Counting-method agreement per sample, tract and tract length",
  modal_by_method = "Modal length per sample by counting method", between = "Between-tract sequences per sample",
  hash = "Parameter hash used for resume"))
write_excel_function(list(timing = timing_df, manifest = manifest), xlsx_path)
dt_compact(timing_df, caption = "Section timing")
dt_compact(manifest, caption = sprintf("module3_output – %s on disk", format_size(file.size(output_path))))
```
